body:
### TL;DR
Exposing ShaderMaterial conversions to the user ([Commit](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/f44bce2ee0774bef4aadffe556ce2016cdc38be9#diff-c2c807db528ea8403dc5953981d00248bc891451924ac938477ea719bffd6632)) allows the user to create ShaderMaterials that store their Shader as a sub_resource instead of a separate path. Because of how ShaderEditorPlugin writes/reads Window_layout, this causes the plugin to request ResourceLoad on a sub_resource path when restoring state before the parent resource has been loaded, throwing the error and failing to restore state.

### My QA: 

The order of events causing this error are:
```
EditorNode::_load_editor_layout
EditorData::set_plugin_window_layout
EditorPlugin::set_window_layout
ResourceLoader::load(::subresource)
```
On specifically the ShaderEditorPlugin. 

The CanvasItemMaterialConversionPlugin, defined and implemented in material_editor_plugin.h / .cpp converts the CanvasItemMaterial to a ShaderMaterial by generating the full Shader Code and storing it as a sub_resource in the resulting ShaderMaterial Resource. This behavior has been around for years, but has been more exposed to users with the addition of Conversion as a built in menu option from file system ([Commit](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/f44bce2ee0774bef4aadffe556ce2016cdc38be9#diff-c2c807db528ea8403dc5953981d00248bc891451924ac938477ea719bffd6632))

This behavior is hypothetically reproducible in earlier builds, but much less straight forward because there isn't a direct way for a user to create a ShaderMaterial that stores its shader as a SubResource, instead of a separate file. Once created though, ShaderEditorPlugin can write a SubResource path to Editor_layout.cfg in ::get_window_layout, which gets read and passed directly to Resource Loader in ::set_window_layout, potentially before the parent resource has been loaded.

This may affect more than just Shaders, there might be other ways with conversions to cause a call to Resource_Load with a sub_resource path?

### Possible Fixes

1. Adjust ShaderEditorPlugin::set_window_layout to detect when path is a sub_resource, and behave differently
2. Adjust ResourceLoader::load to detect when path is a sub_resource, and behave differently
3. Adjust (CanvasItem)MaterialConversionPlugins to create a separate GDShader resource instead of storing as a sub_resource
4. Ignore because this is extremely non-critical

I could fix this myself if I get some clarification on the intended behavior of restoring window layouts that include Sub_Resources!
Does this happen only in 4.4? Can you test in 4.3?

@AThousandShips Verified this behavior also occurs in 4.3 I didn't exactly know how to trigger the conversion in 4.3, but just the TRES file with SubResource is enough to test. Steps I recreated with: 1. Create a new GodotProject 2. Add ShaderMatSubResource.tres to FileSystem 3. View ShaderMatSubResource.tres in inspector, and double click the Shader to open it in the Shader Editor. 4. Close the Editor 5. Re-Open the Editor and open the Project again. 6. The editor throws the error, and fails to restore the viewed Sub_Resource Shader in the Shader Editor Plugin. ``` Godot Engine v4.3.stable.official (c) 2007-present Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur & Godot Contributors. --- Debug adapter server started on port 6006 --- --- GDScript language server started on port 6005 --- Resource file not found: res://ShaderMatSubResource.tres::Shader_dufbx (expected type: ) ``` It appears to me that a few other portions of ShaderEditorPlugin don't behave correctly with Sub_Resources, I also found that deleting ShaderMatSubResource.tres would not remove ShaderMatSubResource.tres::Shader_dufbx from the editor file list.
